verdict.dual_overlaid_ocr_architecture: All 10 sampled LoC llsl PDFs (Vols. 1-62, 19,555 total pages) contain embedded machine-searchable OCR, and all 16 verified statutory specimens carry TWO overlaid 3 Tr invisible OCR passes on the same page: (1) a legacy 2007/2014 Type 1 pass (Times-Roman/Bold/Italic, Helvetica, Courier, WinAnsiEncoding) that preserves small-caps section designators cleanly when the act heading is intact, but merges marginalia into body lines and occasionally drops/truncates running headers ('717' on 38 Stat. 717; 'CH. 68--' on 54 Stat. 847), and (2) a July 2021 Foxit FXPDFA 1.2 / PDF Compressor 8.2.12.20 Type 0 CID pass (/InvisibleOCR, Identity-H) that zones body prose away from marginalia and preserves 16/16 running folios (produced by a separate OCR pass from llsalvol ALTO XML, as shown by running-header differences on 1 Stat. 577), but splits spaced small-caps ('S EC.', 'C HAP.') and occasionally misreads closing brackets ('[CHAPTER 5314', '[CHAPTER 6861'). Blank or un-reprocessed scan frames inside a PDF (e.g. llsl-c48.pdf p. 552 with 0 text and p. 292 with 1 legacy char and no /InvisibleOCR layer) carry zero or one text stream.
